\subsection{Discrimination Collapse Mechanism}
\label{sec:discrimination-collapse}

Head pruning reduces the number of heads contributing to cumulative importance scores, flattening the score distribution. Table~\ref{tab:discrimination-metrics-full} quantifies this effect: the Gini coefficient decreases by $0.030$--$0.081$ (DeepSeek) and $0.010$--$0.020$ (Qwen) after pruning, with consistent negative deltas across all 16 conditions (both models $\times$ 4 sparsity levels $\times$ 2 strategies). The CV delta is likewise negative in all 8 importance-based conditions. The same pattern holds under random eviction, confirming that discrimination collapse is a consequence of head pruning \emph{per se}, not of the eviction strategy. % exp_id: c4_entropy_deepseek, c4_entropy_qwen

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Discrimination collapse under importance-based eviction. $\Delta\mathrm{Gini}$ and $\Delta\mathrm{CV}$ are post-pruning minus baseline; negative values indicate reduced discriminative power.}
\label{tab:discrimination-metrics-full}
\small
\begin{tabular}{llrr}
\toprule
Model & $s$ & $\Delta\mathrm{Gini}$ & $\Delta\mathrm{CV}$ \\
\midrule
DeepSeek & $0.15$ & $-0.030$ & $-0.56$ \\
DeepSeek & $0.20$ & $-0.040$ & $-0.77$ \\
DeepSeek & $0.25$ & $-0.065$ & $-1.29$ \\
DeepSeek & $0.30$ & $-0.081$ & $-1.66$ \\
\midrule
Qwen & $0.15$ & $-0.010$ & $-0.05$ \\
Qwen & $0.20$ & $-0.012$ & $-0.21$ \\
Qwen & $0.25$ & $-0.010$ & $-1.49$ \\
Qwen & $0.30$ & $-0.020$ & $-1.14$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

When importance scores lose discriminability, thresholding degenerates into noise-sensitive selection---functionally approaching biased random eviction. This is phase-dependent: in low-sparsity phases, attention is already broadly distributed, so pruning-induced flattening has maximum impact; in high-sparsity phases, concentration is preserved. Random eviction is immune because its decisions are independent of score quality, explaining $G \approx 1$. The mechanism predicts that any attention-mass-based importance metric should exhibit discrimination collapse under head pruning, while metrics derived from sources independent of attention (e.g., activation magnitude) should produce flatter severity gradients. A secondary entropy redistribution pattern is consistent for DeepSeek but only partially replicates on Qwen (Appendix~\ref{app:entropy-redistribution}). % exp_id: c4_entropy_deepseek, c4_entropy_qwen

\section{Discrimination Collapse Details}
\label{app:discrimination-collapse-details}

The \textbf{Gini coefficient} measures inequality in the importance distribution ($\mathrm{Gini}{=}0$: perfectly uniform; $\mathrm{Gini}{=}1$: maximally concentrated). The \textbf{coefficient of variation} (CV) captures relative dispersion. Table~\ref{tab:discrimination-metrics-full} reports both metrics.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Discrimination collapse under importance-based eviction. $\Delta\mathrm{Gini}$ and $\Delta\mathrm{CV}$ are post-pruning minus baseline; negative values indicate reduced discriminative power. All 8 conditions show consistent negative deltas across both models.}
\label{tab:discrimination-metrics-full}
\small
\begin{tabular}{llrr}
\toprule
Model & $s$ & $\Delta\mathrm{Gini}$ & $\Delta\mathrm{CV}$ \\
\midrule
DeepSeek & $0.15$ & $-0.030$ & $-0.56$ \\
DeepSeek & $0.20$ & $-0.040$ & $-0.77$ \\
DeepSeek & $0.25$ & $-0.065$ & $-1.29$ \\
DeepSeek & $0.30$ & $-0.081$ & $-1.66$ \\
\midrule
Qwen & $0.15$ & $-0.010$ & $-0.05$ \\
Qwen & $0.20$ & $-0.012$ & $-0.21$ \\
Qwen & $0.25$ & $-0.010$ & $-1.49$ \\
Qwen & $0.30$ & $-0.020$ & $-1.14$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Under importance-based eviction, the Gini delta is negative at every sparsity level for both models, with magnitude scaling monotonically with sparsity in DeepSeek. The CV delta is likewise negative in all 8 importance-based conditions. The same pattern holds under random eviction (DeepSeek: $-0.031$ to $-0.073$; Qwen: $-0.019$ to $-0.045$), confirming that discrimination collapse is a consequence of head pruning \emph{per se}, not of the eviction strategy. % exp_id: c4_entropy_deepseek, c4_entropy_qwen

This cross-model consistency establishes discrimination collapse as a robust consequence of compound sparsity. When importance scores lose discriminative power, thresholding the bottom-$s$ fraction becomes noise-sensitive: small perturbations change which positions cross the eviction boundary. In the limit of perfectly uniform scores, importance-based eviction degenerates into an arbitrary selection functionally equivalent to biased random eviction.
